title: Key Takeaways from Nasdaq’s Strong Q1'26 Earnings
summary: Nasdaq’s Q1 earnings report showed that the company delivered exceptional performance, with $1.4 billion in quarterly net revenue. This marks the strongest first quarter start for organic growth in net revenue and operating income since 2021.
body_text: Nasdaq’s ( NDAQ ) Q1 earnings report showed that the company delivered exceptional performance, with $1.4 billion in quarterly net revenue, an increase of 13% on an organic basis, and $1.1 billion in Solutions revenue. This marks the strongest first quarter start for organic growth in net revenue and operating income since 2021. Nasdaq Chair and CEO Adena Friedman said, “We are very pleased with the performance and momentum across Nasdaq as we execute our strategy to modernize markets, power the innovation economy, and build trust in the financial system. ” Key highlights include: Net revenue increased 14% to $1.4 billion year-over-year Annualized Recurring Revenue (ARR) increased 13% to $3.2 billion over the first quarter of 2025 Capital Access Platforms and Market Services both saw 10% organic revenue growth, while Financial Technology revenue growth jumped 18% Annualized SaaS Revenue grew 16% year-over-year on an organic basis, representing 38% of ARR During an interview with CNBC, Friedman said, "What we're finding is our clients are relying on us to help them transform and modernize their operations, their interactions with the markets, and to manage risk more effectively. And we're bringing both cloud and AI to our clients successfully." Here are some additional highlights from the earnings report: Strong Performance Across the Enterprise Financial Technology The Financial Technology division delivered record organic revenue growth of 18% , signing 64 new clients, one cross-sell, and 85 upsells during the quarter. Financial Crime Management Technology saw another robust quarter, signing 58 new small-and-medium bank clients, one enterprise expansion, and 2 enterprise renewals in the quarter. Within Regulatory Technology, AxiomSL signings in the quarter represent more than double the total annualized contract value (ACV) bookings compared to the prior year period with approximately 90% of ACV bookings being cloud deployments. Capital Markets Technology delivered an exceptional quarter with 20% organic revenue growth and 18% organic ARR growth. Market Services Nasdaq Market Services generated record net revenues in the first quarter with record market volumes in U.S. equities and U.S. options, with Nasdaq’s index options revenue more than doubling in that time. Additionally, Nasdaq is making strides forward with its Always-On Markets and its Tokenization programs (more on those below). Capital Access Platforms Nasdaq welcomed 7 of the top 10 IPOs during the quarter, ultimately raising over $5 billion in proceeds. Nasdaq achieved a 71% win rate across eligible U.S. operating companies, direct listings, and SPAC business combinations. Index revenue of $220 million grew 14% on both a reported and organic basis over the first quarter of 2025, with $79 billion of net inflows over the trailing twelve months. Leading the AI Economy Our new AI capabilities are generating client engagement and growth – with more AI innovations in the pipeline. On CNBC, Friedman said, "AI is a core component of all the innovation we're bringing. So whether we can automate workflows for our clients, root out criminals more effectively, AI is an incredible capability that we're bringing across our products." For example, our Agentic AI Workforce is now deployed by more than 500 clients , up over 40% since Investor Day, which was held in February. Later this quarter, Nasdaq Verafin will begin rolling out our new Drug Trafficking analytic, which embeds generative AI directly into our models and synthesizes open source intelligence, social media, and third party research to help clients more effectively detect potential drug trafficking activity. Always-On Markets Early in the second quarter, the SEC approved Nasdaq’s proposal for 23/5 trading . Nasdaq plans to go live with 23/5 trading on December 6, 2026, broadening global investor access to U.S. equities. The SEC approved Nasdaq’s proposal to enable tokenized equity settlement, designed to enhance market liquidity and collateral mobility while maintaining the trust and investor protections of highly regulated public markets. Nasdaq also progressed its tokenization efforts with an equity token design proposal aimed at strengthening the connection between issuers and investors by modernizing governance, transparency, and shareholder engagement. For the complete first quarter 2026 earnings press release, including reconciliations of U.S. GAAP to non-GAAP measures, read Nasdaq’s full Q1 2026 earnings release here . title: Best Medical Record Retrieval Services for Slip and Fall Cases
summary: Compare medical record retrieval options for slip and fall cases and see how Codes Health delivers complete, AI-analyzed records for premises liability claims in a couple of weeks.
body_text: Slip and fall cases hinge on medical documentation that proves injury causation, establishes damages, and defeats pre-existing condition defenses. Yet many law firms wait weeks or longer, sometimes stretching into months, for records that could arrive faster, losing settlement leverage and straining case timelines. This guide profiles the 12 best medical record retrieval services for premises liability cases, explaining what to look for in a provider and how platforms like Codes Health work toward complete, litigation-ready records with AI-powered analysis that flags the buried diagnoses and potential breach-of-care issues that can affect case outcomes. Key Takeaways InsightAce Analytic estimated the medical records retrieval market at $1.1 billion in 2024, projected to reach $2.8 billion by 2034, representing a 10.1% compound annual growth rate Many law firms outsource some or all of the retrieval process to specialized vendors Traditional retrieval can take several weeks and may extend into months when providers are unresponsive, authorizations are deficient, or multiple facilities are involved; some technology-enabled services report shorter average turnaround times Codes Health identifies incomplete or defective authorizations as a leading, often preventable cause of rejected record requests; AI error checking is designed to help prevent delays that would otherwise restart the applicable response period Same-day claims deserve a closer look, since they sometimes describe request submission or access to qualifying EHR records rather than delivery of a complete record set from every provider Codes Health pairs an MIT-educated engineering team with AI purpose-built for litigation-grade medical record analysis, an approach general-purpose AI tools are not designed to replicate without specialized workflows and human verification Understanding the Role of Medical Records in Slip and Fall Cases Medical records serve as the foundation for every slip and fall claim, establishing three critical elements: Causation evidence : Records from the first treatment after an incident create a temporal connection between the fall and resulting injuries. Emergency room notes, urgent care visits, and initial physician evaluations document the mechanism of injury in the patient's own words and capture treating provider causation opinions. Damages documentation : Complete billing records, prescription histories, and treatment progression notes help quantify economic damages while supporting pain and suffering claims. Physical therapy records demonstrate functional limitations, and specialist consultations establish injury severity requiring advanced care. Pre-existing condition defense : Defense attorneys routinely argue that injuries existed before the incident. Comprehensive baseline records covering a case-appropriate period before the fall help establish the plaintiff's prior health status and address alternative causation theories. For slip and fall cases specifically, imaging records (X-rays, MRIs, CT scans) documenting fractures, soft tissue damage, or spinal injuries carry particular weight. Missing even one critical imaging study can undermine settlement negotiations or trial presentation. Challenges of Traditional Medical Record Retrieval for Personal Injury Lawyers Traditional retrieval methods create bottlenecks that delay case resolution and consume staff resources: Extended timelines : Manual processes can take many weeks and, in some cases, months. Certain patient-directed access requests are generally subject to a 30-day federal response period, but attorney and litigation requests may follow different federal or state requirements Provider rejections : Missing signatures, incorrect dates of service, and authorization deficiencies can require resubmission and restart request timelines Incomplete records : Partial deliveries, missing billing records, imaging CDs, or specialist notes require follow-up requests Administrative burden : Managing multiple simultaneous provider relationships can consume substantial staff time, particularly for firms handling numerous concurrent requests Cost unpredictability : Per-page fees and provider charges create billing surprises, especially for hospital records Codes Health identifies incomplete or defective authorizations as a leading, often preventable cause of rejected requests. Missing patient signatures, unclear expiration dates, or unchecked boxes for sensitive records can cause rejection and restart the applicable response period, which varies by jurisdiction and request type. Platforms with AI review are designed to catch these errors before submission, automatically flagging misspellings, missing dates of service, and signature issues that would otherwise cause provider rejections. Same-day claims should be examined carefully. In some cases, they refer to request submission or access to records available through participating EHR networks, rather than delivery of a complete record set from every provider, which can create additional follow-up work when components are missing. Codes Health prioritizes complete documentation, including billing records, imaging, and specialist notes, within a couple of weeks. These challenges compound for slip and fall cases involving multiple treatment facilities: emergency rooms, orthopedic specialists, physical therapists, pain management clinics, and imaging centers. A single premises liability case might require records from 5 to 10 providers, multiplying the administrative complexity. Criteria for Identifying a Leading Medical Records Retrieval Company When evaluating retrieval services for slip and fall cases, prioritize: Speed with completeness : Fast turnaround means little if records arrive incomplete. Look for services emphasizing comprehensive retrieval over same-day partial records. Pre-existing condition handling : Services that flag prior injury mentions help attorneys prepare for defense arguments before they arise. Imaging capabilities : DICOM technology and radiology record expertise matter for slip and fall cases with significant imaging documentation. Security documentation : HIPAA safeguards are essential; independent security reporting, such as SOC 2 Type II or ISO 27001, can provide additional assurance. Pricing transparency : Flat-fee models provide cost predictability; per-page pricing can escalate unexpectedly for voluminous hospital records. Case management integration : Seamless workflows with platforms like Filevine, Clio, SmartAdvocate, and CasePeer reduce manual data entry. AI analysis capabilities : Automated chronologies, diagnosis extraction, and breach-of-care flagging can transform raw records into more actionable case intelligence. The 12 Best Medical Record Retrieval Services for Slip and Fall Cases 1. Codes Health: Best for Complete, AI-Analyzed Records Best For : Firms prioritizing litigation-ready records with AI-powered case insights Turnaround : Complete records in a couple of weeks Pricing : Flat fee (contact Codes Health for details) Codes Health represents a newer generation of AI-powered retrieval platforms, specifically designed for personal injury, mass tort, and medical malpractice litigation. Founded in 2024 and backed by investors including Y Combinator, General Catalyst, Amplify Partners, and Haystack, the platform combines legal expertise with AI. General-purpose AI tools are not independently validated for unsupervised, litigation-grade medical-record review and can produce errors or omit important context. Codes Health is purpose-built for medical-record retrieval and legal review, combining specialized analysis with human verification. Codes Health's MIT-educated engineering team continuously builds out additional workflows and products, ensuring the platform constantly evolves and becomes more comprehensive to meet the changing demands of modern legal practices. Key Features for Slip and Fall Cases : Missing Record Review : AI cross-references patient history to identify documentation gaps before trial Pre-existing condition flagging : Works to surface prior injury mentions relevant to defense preparation Potential breach-of-care indicators : AI flags possible care issues for attorney and expert review Authorization error prevention : Designed to catch missing signatures, incorrect dates, and misspellings before submission AI + human verification : Hybrid model designed to support litigation-grade accuracy "What really struck me about the Codes Health team was how technologically forward they were, using artificial intelligence in ways that none of the other providers could match," notes Charles Brown, Managing Partner at Daly & Black P.C. The platform works across claims clearinghouse connections, custodian integrations, and proprietary provider networks while offering custom integrations with CRM platforms and medical software for high-volume customers. 2. Tavrn: Best for End-to-End Case Workflow Best For : Firms wanting retrieval through demand letter automation Turnaround : Under 24 hours for chronologies; a company-reported 70% faster than standard methods Pricing : Plans start at $299.99 per month for 20 requests, with additional requests priced at $20 each; provider charges may apply Tavrn offers workflow automation from intake through demand letter generation, with nationwide retrieval services for personal injury law firms. Key Features for Slip and Fall Cases : AI-generated medical chronologies delivered in under 24 hours Automated demand letter generation Pre-organized records with tags and duplicate removal Nationwide retrieval coverage through electronic and traditional provider outreach HIPAA and SOC 2 Type II compliance The platform's workflow breadth, spanning intake, retrieval, chronology, and demand letters, suits firms seeking comprehensive automation rather than retrieval-only solutions. 3. Lexitas Legal Services: Best for Enterprise Provider Networks Best For : High-volume firms needing nationwide coverage Turnaround : 30 to 45 days average Pricing : Contact Lexitas for a quote Lexitas operates multiple locations nationwide with an extensive provider network coverage and more than 300 employees. Key Features for Slip and Fall Cases : Record Insights® platform with AI-enabled automated summaries (confirm separately whether legal nurse consultant chronologies are included and at what cost) 98% completion rate Court-compliant formatting for trial readiness Dedicated account management Lexitas was selected for Zantac MDL retrieval work and reports processing more than 157,000 record sets, demonstrating scale capabilities for complex litigation. 4. ChartRequest (CaseBinder): Best for Customer Service Best For : Firms valuing high-touch support with technology Turnaround : Fast and compliant (specific timeline not published) Pricing : Contact for ongoing pricing; ChartRequest currently advertises a limited introductory rate of $35 per request for 90 days Founded in 2012 in Atlanta, ChartRequest maintains a network of more than 12,000 healthcare organizations and reports a 4.9-out-of-5 Google rating on its website. Key Features for Slip and Fall Cases : CaseBinder white-glove service for law firms Real-time status tracking via mobile app and dashboard Expedited processing for urgent deadlines SOC 2 and ISO 27001 compliance Case management system integrations The hybrid approach combining automation with human oversight suits firms wanting technology efficiency with personal support for complex slip and fall cases. 5. Records On Time (Rob Levine Legal Solutions): Best for Predictable Per-Record Pricing Best For : Cost-conscious firms wanting predictable pricing Turnaround : Traditional retrieval averages approximately 21 to 23 days; qualifying EHR records from a network of more than 400,000 providers may be available in as little as one day Pricing : $49.95 per record plus applicable provider fees (waived for qualifying EHR retrievals); no monthly subscription required Built by personal injury attorney Rob Levine, this platform reports a 99% completion rate and retrieving approximately 130,000 records annually. Key Features for Slip and Fall Cases : Provider fees waived for qualifying EHR retrievals Integrations with major case management systems, including Neos, Needles, SmartAdvocate, Litify, Filevine, Clio, and CasePeer Rapid EHR access from a network of more than 400,000 providers SOC 2 certified, HIPAA-compliant No contracts required The attorney-designed platform structures pricing around a per-record fee with waived provider charges for qualifying electronic retrievals, which can help with budget predictability. 6. American Retrieval: Best for Fast Traditional Turnaround Best For : Firms needing reliable speed without AI complexity Turnaround : Company-reported 15-day average Pricing : Flat rate; confirm current charges for unsuccessful or no-record requests directly with the company Operating since 1993, American Retrieval reports a consistent average turnaround of approximately 15 days. Its Datavant integration provides access to a network the company says covers approximately 55% of U.S. healthcare providers. Key Features for Slip and Fall Cases : OCR technology for full electronic search Searchable and shareable records HIPAA-compliant portal Acquired by U.S. Legal Support in January 2025 7. U.S. Legal Support: Best for Maximum Enterprise Scale Best For : Large firms with high-volume, multi-state caseloads Turnaround : The company states a goal of approximately 30 to 40 days, depending on provider response and request complexity Pricing : Request-specific quote U.S. Legal Support operates at significant scale with extensive provider relationships across all 50 states. Key Features for Slip and Fall Cases : SOC 2 Type II certification verified by independent audits 24/7 secure portal access Nearly 30 years of experience Full litigation support suite (court reporting, translations, trial services) Comprehensive HIPAA compliance U.S. Legal Support publishes industry commentary on medical record retrieval trends. 8. YoCierge: Best for Case Management Integrations Best For : Firms with established tech stacks needing seamless workflows Turnaround : Same-day order submission (before 4pm) Pricing : Flat fee (no per-page charges) Founded in 2017, YoCierge retrieves nearly 400,000 medical records annually through a concierge-style service model. Key Features for Slip and Fall Cases : Integrations with major legal case-management systems, including Filevine, Clio, SmartAdvocate, Neos, and Smokeball Integrated DICOM viewer for radiology and imaging YoSign e-authorization system SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and CARIN-related compliance information Flat fee regardless of page count Same-day processing refers to request submission timing, not record delivery. Actual retrieval depends on provider response times. 9. Record Retrieval Solutions (RRS): Best for Transparent Pricing Best For : Budget-conscious firms wanting published rates Turnaround : Approximately 15 to 16 days on average, according to the company Pricing : $45 retrieval fee per request, plus provider and copy charges passed through without markup With more than 30 years of record-retrieval experience, RRS serves personal injury, mass tort, medical malpractice, insurance, and other sectors, and offers clearly published base pricing. Key Features for Slip and Fall Cases : Published base pricing helps reduce billing surprises Medical record summarization and indexable chronologies Secure "one-stop-shop" online portal Dedicated account management for high-volume practices HIPAA-compliant with consistent regulatory updates RRS's personal injury and mass tort experience means familiarity with slip and fall documentation requirements. 10. Compex Legal Services: Best for Established Track Record Best For : Firms valuing proven stability and longevity Turnaround : Contact for an estimate Pricing : Contact for a request-specific quote With more than 50 years of operation, Compex is a long-operating national firm, serving more than 5,000 law firms and approximately 350 insurance carriers. Key Features for Slip and Fall Cases : Asabell AI-powered summarization Tech-enabled retrieval with comprehensive tracking Full-service suite including IME interface and deposition reporting Coverage across all 50 states Named a Top 10 Legal Technology Solutions Provider by CIOCoverage in 2023 The large client network points to an established, longstanding service history. 11. MCS Group: Best for Medical Imaging Best For : Cases with significant X-ray, MRI, or CT scan documentation Turnaround : Not publicly specified Pricing : Custom Operating for more than 40 years, MCS Group specializes in advanced medical imaging, relevant for slip and fall cases, documenting fractures, spinal injuries, and soft tissue damage. Key Features for Slip and Fall Cases : Advanced DICOM imaging tools for X-rays, MRIs, PET scans, CT scans MCSDirect platform for real-time tracking Medical record analysis and chronological summarization National reach with regional offices For premises liability cases where imaging proves injury severity and timing, MCS Group's DICOM expertise provides particular value. 12. Ontellus: Best for Multi-State Litigation Best For : Firms handling complex jurisdictional matters Turnaround : Fast (specific timeline not published) Pricing : Custom Among the larger retrieval firms in North America, Ontellus serves both plaintiff law firms and insurance defense with SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliance. Key Features for Slip and Fall Cases : Nationwide coverage across all 50 states Secure portal for document delivery Authorization management and provider communication High-volume enterprise capabilities Multi-state litigation expertise The dual-market focus (plaintiff and defense) points to broad industry experience and established provider relationships. Cost-Benefit Analysis: Investing in Premium Record Retrieval Traditional in-house processing can consume substantial staff time coordinating requests, tracking responses, and following up with providers, with no automated workflow to offset that burden. Legacy retrieval services can reduce some of that burden through outsourcing, though staff still typically handle oversight and review. AI-powered solutions like Codes Health are designed to reduce repetitive staff work by automating request review, provider follow-up, status tracking, and record organization, while working toward complete records in a couple of weeks rather than months. The amount of time saved depends on request volume and the firm's existing workflow. For slip and fall cases specifically, faster, more complete retrieval can support: Earlier demand package preparation More time for expert review before statute of limitations pressure Stronger case preparation ahead of negotiations with defense counsel Higher case velocity without proportional staff growth Frequently Asked Questions How quickly can medical records be retrieved for a slip and fall case? Traditional manual processes can take several weeks and may extend into months when providers are unresponsive or authorizations are deficient. Some technology-enabled services report shorter average turnaround times. Same-day partial records are sometimes possible through EHR integrations, but complete documentation, including billing records, imaging CDs, and specialist notes, often takes several weeks and depends on provider responsiveness, request scope, authorization quality, and applicable legal requirements. What insights can AI provide from medical records in personal injury claims? AI platforms can extract diagnoses, treatments, and medical history from unstructured records. For slip and fall cases, Codes Health surfaces potential breach-of-care indicators, treatment recommendations and documentation relevant to future-expense analysis, pre-existing conditions, and chronological treatment history for attorney and expert review. Is medical record retrieval HIPAA compliant? Reputable services maintain appropriate HIPAA safeguards. Enterprise-grade providers often add independent security reporting such as SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and secure portal access. Always verify certifications before sharing patient information. Can a retrieval service help identify missing records for a slip and fall claim? Yes. Missing Record Review capabilities cross-reference patient history against received records to visualize gaps in documentation. This helps support completeness before trial, addressing potential defense arguments about undisclosed treatment or hidden pre-existing conditions. How does faster medical record retrieval impact slip and fall settlement outcomes? Complete, well-organized records can strengthen case evaluation, support demand preparation, and help counsel address causation and damages issues earlier. The effect on settlement value depends on the facts of each case. Faster retrieval also provides more time for expert review, which can support causation opinions and damages calculations.

title: Kaiser Aluminum Corporation Announces Quarterly Dividend Payment
summary: FRANKLIN, Tenn.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Kaiser Aluminum Corporation (NASDAQ:KALU) today announced that its Board of Directors has declared a…...
body_text: Kaiser Aluminum Corporation Announces Quarterly Dividend Payment July 13, 2026 4:30pm EDT FRANKLIN, Tenn.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Kaiser Aluminum Corporation (NASDAQ:KALU) today announced that its Board of Directors has declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.77 per share. The dividend will be payable on August 14, 2026 to stockholders of record as of the close of business on July 24, 2026. About Kaiser Aluminum Corporation Kaiser Aluminum Corporation, headquartered in Franklin, Tenn., is a leading producer of semi-fabricated specialty aluminum products, serving customers worldwide with highly-engineered solutions for aerospace and high-strength, packaging, general engineering, automotive extrusions, and other industrial applications. The Company’s North American facilities produce value-added plate, sheet, coil, extrusions, rod, bar, tube, and wire products, adhering to traditions of quality, innovation, and service that have been key components of the culture since the Company was founded in 1946. The Company’s stock is included in the Russell 2000® index and the S&P Small Cap 600® index. Available Information For more information, please visit the Company’s website at www.kaiseraluminum.com . The website includes a section for investor relations under which the Company provides notifications of news or announcements regarding its financial performance, including Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filings, investor events, and earnings and other press releases. In addition, all Company filings submitted to the SEC are available through a link to the section of the SEC’s website at www.sec.gov , which includes: Annual Reports on Form 10-K, Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q, Current Reports on Form 8-K and Proxy Statements for the Company’s annual stockholders’ meetings, and other information statements as filed with the SEC. In addition, the Company provides a webcast of its quarterly earnings calls and certain events in which management participates or hosts with members of the investment community. title: The 7 best AI photo editing software for product photos
summary: This is a detailed guide to the best photo editors to check out in 2024. Each one caters to different needs, editing skills, and budget.
body_text: AI photo-editing software presents an opportunity and a challenge for e‑commerce teams, whether you’re a business owner, marketer or agency. These photo editing tools can do more than make high-quality edits; the best AI photo editors increase speed and scale in ways that make a real difference for your business. Imagine if you could edit your next product catalog in just a few clicks, or use a single photo to generate assets across multiple platforms. You could go to market faster and use that extra time to grow your business—all while seeing higher conversions. Your competitors are already using AI product photography tools . Now it’s your turn. The challenge lies in finding the right tool. What is the best AI photo editing software for product photography? We took a close look at the top AI photo-editing tools and analyzed their software and capabilities for e‑commerce workflows. Key takeaways AI features are standard across most photo editors, but the ones that matter for e‑commerce teams (such as background removal, object removal, outpainting, and upscaling) aren’t ubiquitous. Workflow fit is key to making the most of an AI photo editor. Depending on your business and needs, this could include features like batch editing, templates, RAW file processing, and/or mobile and desktop compatibility. Pricing model types vary across AI photo editors. Many offer subscription models that allow you to cancel at any time, while others are one-time purchases for perpetual licenses. Best AI photo editing software for e‑commerce Tool Best for Pricing Compatibility Photoroom Creating production-ready visuals for e‑commerce Free plan available Pro: $12.99/month or $90/year Max: $34.99/month or $251.88/year Ultra: From $99/month or $990/yea iOS, Android, iPad, macOS, Windows Adobe Photoshop Precision and heavy manual control Plans start at $22.99/month with an annual subscription Windows and macOS Adobe Lightroom Batch edits and integrations into existing Adobe Suite products Plans start at $11.99/month with an annual commitment Web, iOS, Android, iPad, macOS, Windows GIMP Creating custom interfaces and tools Free Linux, macOS, Windows Luminar Neo Quick enhancement of product images Perpetual-use licenses start at $99 for desktop-only use. macOS, Windows, iOS, Android, Chrome OS Canva Heavily branded product photography Free plans are available AI tools are included with Pro plans, starting at $15/month or $10/month when billed annually iPad, macOS, Windows, iOS, Android Capture One Pro In the moment, photo edits on professional sets Plans start at $26/month or $17/month when billed annually iOS, Android, iPad, macOS, Windows Our criteria for choosing an AI photo editor With so many AI editing tools available, the key is finding one that matches how you actually work. The best tools simplify your existing product photography workflows, making them both faster and more efficient—all while improving the overall quality of your images. How do you know which tool will help you do just that? We’ve evaluated each AI photo editor based on the following key factors: User interface: Intuitive layouts, clear menus, and straightforward workflows. E‑commerce specific capabilities: Features that merchants need, like background removal, batch editing , and outpainting, and marketplace templates. Compatibility: With various operating systems (Windows, macOS, Linux) and support for different file formats, especially RAW. The best AI photo editors 1. Photoroom What it does best: Photoroom’s AI-powered image editor is built specifically for e‑commerce. Teams of all sizes use Photoroom to simplify catalog and listing workflows and create production-ready product visuals at scale. Best use case: You’re an enterprise-level sports gear company that regularly releases new, seasonal product catalogs. Discover how Photoroom’s Enterprise API can automatically remove backgrounds, adjust lighting, and upload photos to your content management system. Pros : Background removal and generation allow you to reuse images across multiple platforms and contexts. Create lifestyle photography, studio shots, and flat-lay images from a single photo. Photoroom has a wide range of AI-powered tools trained specifically on e‑commerce images. Tools like Instant Shadows (for adding realistic shadows), Ghost Mannequin (for capturing fit and drape), Virtual Models (for showcasing products on people), and Recolor (for capturing new colorways) are beginner-friendly and provide professional results. The tool’s enterprise API integrates with existing workflows on platforms like Zapier, Figma, and Shopify. Batch editing lets you apply the same edits to up to 500 photos at once, reducing manual work, errors, and editing time. Photoroom offers multiple export options, including resolutions and file formats (PNG, JPEG, and WebP), suitable for various platforms. 2. Adobe Photoshop What it does best: Adobe Photoshop is a go-to editing software for marketing teams and agencies that require deep manual control, precision, and custom product visuals. Best use case: You are a photo editor for a marketing team of a large fashion brand. You use Photoshop to edit lifestyle imagery for a new catalog, focusing on features like retouching and advanced photo manipulation. Pros: Adobe Photoshop offers a range of features for precise editing, such as layers, masks, and selection tools. These features allow users to make intricate adjustments to their photos. Strong retouching capabilities, with tools for removing blemishes, correcting colors, and restoring old photographs. Best for e‑commerce teams who frequently work with models or on imperfect sets. AI features like Content-Aware Fill, Generative Fill, and auto-tagging reduce the time it takes to make complex edits. Adobe Photoshop is an industry standard for photo editing, but its complex interface and in-depth tools lead to heavy, time-consuming workflows that are difficult to replicate across catalogs. Learn more: Photoroom vs Photoshop: which tool wins for e‑commerce visual marketing? 3. Adobe Lightroom What it does best: Adobe Lightroom’s beginner-friendly batch editing capabilities allow e‑commerce teams to correct product and brand photos at scale. Best use case : A recent studio photography shoot for a new catalog has poor lighting and contrast. Instead of manually editing each photo, apply exposure adjustments and color balance edits across the entire catalog. Pros : All edits in Adobe Lightroom are non-destructive: the original image remains untouched, and changes can be reversed or modified at any time. Integrates with Photoshop and other Adobe apps, allowing existing Adobe users to integrate Lightroom into their editing workflows. Adept at handling RAW files, offering extensive tools to adjust exposure, contrast, color balance, and more while preserving high image quality and color consistency. Adobe Lightroom is a strong tool for e‑commerce teams looking to make batch edits, but without compositing tools or automation capabilities, it doesn’t support more complex photo edits at scale. 4. GIMP What it does best: GIMP (GNU Image Manipulation Program) is a free, manual image editor with features that rival those of expensive professional software. Best use case: You are a student running a resale business out of your dorm room. Instead of investing in a costly photo editor (or risk losing sales to more experienced sellers), you use GIMP to achieve professional-level product listings at no cost. Pros: GIMP offers advanced image manipulation tools, including photo retouching, selection, image composition, and image authoring. Similar to Photoshop, GIMP supports layers and masks, enabling complex compositions and adjustments without altering the original image. Users can customize the interface to suit their workflow, arranging tools and panels to their preference. If you have an advanced understanding of photo-editing software, this can significantly improve your workflows. GIMP is an attractive free option, but it has a steep learning curve for teams without professional photo-editing experience. And unlike Photoroom, GIMP lacks features that streamline workflows. 5. Luminar Neo What it does best: Luminar Neo’s advanced AI filters and tools quickly enhance product images with professional-level results. Best use case: You are a jewelry designer preparing to launch your new collection on Shopify, but the photos you took at home aren’t as high-quality as your products. Use Luminar Neo’s AI filters to enhance lighting or colors, and remove or replace background objects. Pros: AI photo-editing features and filters like Sky Replacement, AI Structure, and AI Enhance allow e‑commerce teams to dramatically improve product photos with minimal effort. Luminar Neo supports up to 1000 cameras and multiple file types, including RAF, ORF, and NEF. The tool’s interface is easy to navigate, making it beginner-friendly without sacrificing advanced editing tools. Luminar Neo’s AI photo-editing tools are easy to use for one-off edits, but e‑commerce teams that need to regularly edit product photos at scale might find the tool’s lack of batch editing and automated workflows limiting. 6. Canva What it does best: Canva’s brand kit templates lend themselves to consistent, high-quality product photography without extensive editing knowledge. Best use case: You’re an artisan hot sauce maker with a strong visual brand. Use Canva’s brand kit to apply your logo and signature colors across each one of your product photos for every single launch. Pros: Canva’s Magic Studio offers a suite of AI-powered tools that e‑commerce teams need to create product images, including Background Remover and Magic Expand, an outpainting tool for enlarging product images. In addition to brand kits, Canva Pro users can create templates that multiple team members can access, making it easier to standardize product photography for larger teams. Beginner editors find Canva’s drag-and-drop interface easy to navigate and use without much additional training or tutorials. Canva is a strong option for e‑commerce teams looking to create brand-forward product photography, but its AI workflows are highly manual and can’t be applied to multiple images at once. Learn More: Photoroom vs Canva: which tool fits your editing needs? 7. Capture One Pro What it does best: Capture One Pro is studio-grade product-photography software that is especially good at RAW handling and tethered shooting, making it a preferred choice for studio environments where instant feedback is important. Best use case : You’re overseeing a lifestyle shoot for a client’s newest home decor line. Use Capture One Pro to test lighting and edits as you set up your shots. Pros: Capture One Pro is renowned for its excellent RAW file processing, delivering high-quality results with great detail and color accuracy. Asset management features, including catalogs and sessions, help teams efficiently organize and manage large photo libraries. The software provides sophisticated color grading tools, including color wheels, curves, and an advanced color editor, allowing for precise color adjustments. Capture One Pro is a favorite among professional photo editors, but it's a heavy, expensive tool compared to other options on the market that offer stronger e-commerce-specific features. How to choose the best photo editor for your needs The best AI photo editor for your unique needs is the one that matches your skill level, is compatible with your most common edits and workflows, and fits comfortably within your budget. Here’s a guide to help you make an informed decision. Step 1: Identify your skill level Some tools are easier for beginners than others, offering intuitive templates and AI features that simplify complex editing processes. If you feel comfortable with AI photo editing tools , you might focus more on advanced processing capabilities or enterprise integrations to grow your business further. Step 2. Determine your editing needs Maybe you’re a Shopify merchant who wants their listings to stand out on the Shop app, or you’re a one-person marketing team who spends hours editing product images. Whatever your use case, ask yourself: which edits do you make the most often? Which would you make if you had the capabilities? The combination of these two will determine which features to look for in an AI image editing software. Step 3. Consider your workflow Your AI photo-editing tool should work together with your other creative tools, programs, and processes. For example, if you regularly upload dozens of new products to Amazon, use a tool like Photoroom, which offers batch editing and Amazon templates. If you need to edit photos on the go, choose software that offers mobile versions or cloud synchronization for consistent editing across devices. Step 4. Evaluate your budget For budget-friendly editing without compromising quality, consider a subscription-based photo editor. You can plan for monthly payments and cancel when you no longer need it. If you’re ready to commit to one tool, an annual subscription is usually cheaper in the long run than monthly payments. Step 5. Test before you commit Many paid photo editing apps offer free trials. Use these to test the tool’s capabilities and determine whether they meet your needs. You can also watch demos and read tutorials to understand the software’s capabilities and workflow before making a decision. Match the editor to your workflow Any AI photo editing software can help you create high-quality product images, but not every tool can help you create them at scale. Along with budget and ease of use, the best AI photo editor for your e‑commerce business will simplify and unify your workflows—saving you time and creating new opportunities for growth. Among AI photo-editing tools, Photoroom stands out for its unique features and workflows designed for e‑commerce teams. Not only is the tool’s AI trained on e‑commerce images, but the easy-to-navigate interface, one-click editing tools, and features like batch edit, allow you to create your best product images yet, faster and at scale. Download Photoroom from the App Store or Google Play , or use the web app to get started. Frequently asked questions What is AI photo editing software for e‑commerce? AI photo-editing software for e‑commerce automates product image workflows, including background removal, resizing, color correction, and format conversion . Unlike general photo editors, e-commerce-focused tools prioritize speed, consistency, and scale over creative flexibility. They help sellers prepare catalog-ready images faster by handling repetitive tasks that would otherwise require manual editing across hundreds of SKUs. Can AI photo editors handle large product catalogs? Yes, but capabilities vary significantly across software. Batch editing is the key differentiator. Tools like Photoroom and Lightroom let you apply identical edits across multiple images with just a few clicks, while others like Canva and Luminar Neo require manual, image-by-image workflows. Look for tools that support batch processing, reusable templates, and API integrations to avoid bottlenecks during seasonal launches or inventory updates. How do AI photo editors help adapt images for different marketplaces? Marketplace-ready tools automate format adaptation—resizing a single product shot for platforms (e.g, Amazon , Shopify, Etsy) and use cases (lifestyle, studio shots, overhead images). Advanced editors like Photoroom include platform-specific templates that can be combined with other AI editing features to create scalable workflows. For example, use Background Remover to clean up product photography, Recolor to showcase new SKUs, Virtual Model to create lifestyle imagery, and Batch to apply these edits across every image. The result is marketplace-compliant photography that stands out against competitors. What makes an AI photo editor suitable for product listings? Listing-specific features matter more than general AI capabilities. The editor you pick should meaningfully simplify your product photography workflow for catalogs and listings. Tools to look for include background removal for clean product shots, consistent lighting and shadow generation, upscaling for high-resolution marketplace requirements, and one-click formatting for various platforms. The editor should also prioritize production speed over creative effects. Features like batch mode, reusable backgrounds, and export presets save more time than artistic filters when managing active inventory. Is AI photo editing reliable for commercial product images? Yes, although some tools offer more consistent edits than others. AI photo editing is especially reliable when the tool is trained on commercial imagery. E-commerce-specific editors like Photoroom deliver consistent, marketplace-compliant results because the AI understands product photography contexts. General-purpose AI tools may produce inconsistent outputs that require manual correction. Test any editor with your actual product images before committing, and focus on output quality across different product categories and materials.

(NASDAQ: PGY) (“Pagaya”), a global technology company delivering
body_text: PDF Version 140.5 KB Upsized to $750 million, RPM 2026-4 is now the largest Auto ABS deal in Pagaya’s history, following two other company-record-breaking deals earlier this year NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Jul. 16, 2026-- Pagaya Technologies Ltd. (NASDAQ: PGY) (“Pagaya”), a global technology company delivering AI-driven product solutions for the financial ecosystem, today announced the closing of RPM 2026-4, a $750 million upsized auto asset-backed securitization (ABS). This marks Pagaya’s fourth fully pre-funded auto ABS transaction of 2026 and its largest to date, bringing the total amount of pre-funded auto ABS raised this year to $2.25 billion. Notably, this transaction features Pagaya's inaugural excess spread tranche, designed to optimize cash flow distribution and capture portfolio residual returns. "Executing our largest ever RPM deal underscores the continued acceleration of the broader Pagaya auto platform,” said Sahil Chandiramani, Head of Capital Markets at Pagaya. “The number of investors participating in our RPM shelf has more than doubled since the beginning of last year - a testament to our ability to consistently offer attractive, fit-to-market structures backed by high-quality collateral from the nation's largest auto lenders." Forty-one unique investors participated in this transaction, including six new investors to Pagaya’s broader ABS platform and seven new investors to Pagaya’s auto ABS shelf. Since 2018, Pagaya has raised more than $40 billion across 92 ABS transactions to fund loan originations across multiple products, including personal loan and auto. About Pagaya Technologies Pagaya (NASDAQ: PGY) is a global technology company making life-changing financial products and services available to more people nationwide, as it reshapes the financial services ecosystem. By using machine learning, a vast data network and an AI-driven approach, Pagaya provides consumer credit and other products for its partners, their customers, and investors. Its proprietary API and capital solutions integrate into its network of partners to deliver seamless user experiences and greater access to the mainstream economy. For more information, visit pagaya.com . title: Making a Difference Together Through Community Impact
summary: By Sophia Pösl, HR Generalist Creating a positive impact extends beyond the work we do for our customers. Through NovantaCARES, our employees dedicate their time and energy to supporting the communities where we live and work. During the first half of the year, our team in Wackersdorf, Germany, completed five volunteer initiatives focused on community support, environmental stewardship, and local […]
body_text: By Sophia Pösl, HR Generalist Creating a positive impact extends beyond the work we do for our customers. Through NovantaCARES, our employees dedicate their time and energy to supporting the communities where we live and work. During the first half of the year, our team in Wackersdorf, Germany, completed five volunteer initiatives focused on community support, environmental stewardship, and local partnerships. Each activity demonstrated the values that guide our culture and our commitment to making a difference together. A longstanding example is our partnership with the Perschen Open-Air Museum. Employees volunteer to help maintain and restore the site’s barefoot trail, a project that has become a tradition for the team. Even in challenging weather conditions, volunteers continue to show the dedication and teamwork that make these efforts successful. The team also supported the Schwandorf food bank (Tafel), helping sort and distribute food for individuals and families in need. These experiences provide a meaningful opportunity to connect with the community while reinforcing the importance of empathy with service. Environmental responsibility is another important focus. Through an annual clean-up initiative, employees help improve local public spaces while contributing to broader sustainability efforts. The activity aligns with the spirit of Earth Day and demonstrates how collective action can create lasting benefits for the community. Beyond organized volunteer events, employees also pursue individual acts of service. From helping maintain local playgrounds to supporting other community needs, these efforts reflect a culture where responsibility and care extend beyond the workplace. Over the years, the Wackersdorf team has become a trusted partner to local organizations. Those relationships continue to inspire new opportunities to serve and create meaningful impact. Together, these efforts demonstrate what is possible when employees come together with a shared commitment to making a difference. Through NovantaCARES, we are proud to support stronger communities and help build a brighter future for all.

title: Vertiv Introduces New Infrastructure Products for Edge Deployments
summary: Vertiv today introduced power and rack products to meet the unique challenges of the network edge, including the need for rapid deployment, remote monitoring and management, and end-to-end service.
body_text: Columbus, OH [August 15, 2018] – Vertiv today introduced power and rack products to meet the unique challenges of the network edge, including the need for rapid deployment, remote monitoring and management, and end-to-end service. These products include the Vertiv™ Liebert® PSI5 uninterruptible power supply (UPS) system, the Vertiv™ VR rack, and Vertiv™ rack power distribution units (rack PDUs) with features to meet the needs of many edge sites. All products will be stocked in North America for quicker availability to help speed deployments. The launch of these products further expands the Vertiv portfolio of edge solutions. The breadth of product and service choices is critical at the edge, where IT needs may be different from site to site and constantly evolving. A single vendor partner that can provide end-to-end infrastructure solutions and support presents strong value to companies that require edge deployment, but do not have the resources or expertise to sustain this business model. “As we continue to monitor the evolution of the edge and further define the needs of various edge archetypes , it is clear that one of the key factors for success at the edge is flexibility,” said Angie McMillin, vice president of offering management for Vertiv in the Americas. “With this launch, we add to an edge portfolio that delivers that flexibility by giving our customers options for their edge deployments. By building a broader offering, Vertiv is helping businesses own the edge.” The Vertiv Liebert PSI5 high performance, line-interactive UPS joins the Vertiv portfolio of rack/tower configurable UPS. This single-phase UPS system is designed for the small spaces and high rack power densities common at the edge. The 2U UPS can be remotely monitored and controlled, has multiple options to meet runtime requirements, and is available with the optional Vertiv Power Assurance Package - a lifecycle support plan that includes installation and startup, on-site service, remote oversight and a 5-year protection plan. The Vertiv VR rack is a robust and flexible rack solution that allows for rapid deployment. Eight standard sizes are available, all featuring a frame design that delivers about 2.5 inches of additional useable depth compared to similar sized racks, for ease of installation and maintenance of critical equipment. The rack is complemented by a variety of tool-less accessories to help speed deployment and facilitate rack management. The new Vertiv rack PDUs are available in basic and intelligent models, stocked for rapid delivery. Intelligent models can monitor input power to plus or minus 1 percent accuracy, in addition to standard readings including amps, volts, watts, kWh and power factor. Switched models are available with the ability to monitor and control input power at each outlet, hot swappable modules to allow rapid change in the field, and patented U-lock receptacles that lock any cord in place to eliminate unintentional disconnection are among other notable features. All models have the industry’s best 5 year warranty, when registered within 120 days of purchase, and may also be supported by the Vertiv Distribution Assurance Package lifecycle support, which includes startup, installation, maintenance, repair, emergency response and other features. To learn more about other Vertiv offerings, please visit www.Vertiv.com . About Vertiv Vertiv designs, builds and services critical infrastructure that enables vital applications for data centers, communication networks and commercial and industrial facilities. Formerly Emerson Network Power, Vertiv supports today’s growing mobile and cloud computing markets with a portfolio of power, thermal and infrastructure management solutions including the Chloride®, Liebert®, NetSure™ and Trellis ™ brands. For more information, visit Vertiv.com . Contact: Vince McMorrow 614-383-1622 Vince.McMorrow@Fahlgren.com
